target_moa.text: Suvorexant is a highly selective dual orexin receptor antagonist that blocks the binding of the wake-promoting neuropeptides orexin A and orexin B to receptors OX1R and OX2R, thereby inhibiting activation of wakefulness-promoting neurons and facilitating transition from wake to sleep.

citations.quote: Suvorexant is a new chemical entity that is suggested to act as a highly selective antagonist for orexin receptors OX1R and OX2R.
Suvorexant is suggested to transiently block the binding of the wake-promoting neurotransmitters orexin A and orexin B to their receptors OX1R and OX2R.
By doing so, suvorexant inhibits activation of wakefulness-promoting neurons of the arousal system, and facilitates transitions from wake to sleep.

key_safety.text: The most common adverse reaction (>=5% and at least twice placebo) was somnolence (BELSOMRA 7%; placebo 3%). Daytime somnolence with impaired alertness and motor coordination (including impaired driving) is the principal risk and increases with dose. Other adverse reactions included headache (7% vs 6% placebo), dizziness (3% vs 2%), diarrhea, dry mouth, abnormal dreams, and cough.

vote.text: The Peripheral and Central Nervous System Advisory Committee (May 22, 2013) found substantial evidence of efficacy for sleep onset (12 yes/4 no) and sleep maintenance (16 yes/0 no), and that the 15 mg and 20 mg doses were acceptably safe (15 yes/3 no); the committee was divided on the safety of the 30 mg and 40 mg doses (7 yes/8 no).

citations.quote: The suvorexant NDA was considered at a meeting of the Peripheral and Central Nervous System Advisory Committee on May 22, 2013, and had the following major recommendations:
Most Committee members agreed that there was substantial evidence of efficacy for suvorexant at the doses studied, for both sleep onset (12 yes/4 no) and sleep maintenance (16 yes/0 no).
Most Committee members agreed that doses of 15 mg and 20 mg were acceptably safe, by a vote of 15 yes/ 3 no.
The Committee was of divided opinion about if safety was adequate for the 30 mg and 40 mg doses, with 7 voting 'yes', and 8 voting 'no'.

detail.text: The NDA was dated and received August 30, 2012 and approved August 13, 2014 without a prior Complete Response Letter; the review ultimately recommended approval with lower (5, 10, 15, 20 mg) strengths.
